draft.title: Contested interpretations
card: An interpretation is a historian's explanation of the past. Historians sometimes disagree strongly about what happened or how to describe it.
They may use different evidence. One historian may rely on official records, while another uses oral histories or other sources.
They may ask different questions, or hold different values about what matters most. Language can differ too, such as how to describe frontier conflict.
A disagreement does not mean the past did not happen. It shows that evidence has to be read and explained by people.
draft.remember: Historians can disagree because of different evidence, questions or values, not because the past is invented.

a.q: Two historians describe frontier conflict differently. What is a likely reason?
opts: They used different evidence or asked different questions
One of them has decided that the events never happened
They both used exactly the same sources and questions
Historians can only disagree when someone has made an error
a.why: Different evidence, questions or values can lead to different interpretations. Disagreement does not mean the events are denied, and it does not always mean someone has made an error.
a.clue: Think about what each historian started with.

b.q: Priya reads two books on a colonial town. One uses police records. The other uses oral histories from local families. They describe the same events very differently. What best explains this?
opts: Each used evidence that gave a different point of view
Only the book using police records can be a history
The oral histories prove the police records were forged
The authors must be wrong, as true accounts cannot differ
b.why: Police records and oral histories can show different sides of the same events, so the books reach different interpretations. Neither type of source is automatically the only valid one, and a difference does not prove forgery.
b.clue: Compare whose view each type of source records.

a.best: They used different evidence or asked different questions

b.best: Each used evidence that gave a different point of view

problems.detail: Every wrong option is extreme or absolute ('exactly the same', 'can only', 'never happened'). The right option is the only measured one, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Contested interpretations
card: An interpretation is a historian's explanation of the past. Historians sometimes disagree strongly about what happened or how to describe it.
They may use different evidence. One historian may rely on official records, while another uses oral histories, which are people's spoken accounts. Both are kinds of evidence.
They may ask different questions, or hold different values about what matters most. Language can differ too, such as how to describe frontier conflict.
A disagreement does not mean the past did not happen or has changed. It usually comes from how people choose and explain evidence, not from simple mistakes or made-up events.
proposal.remember: Historians can disagree because of different evidence, questions or values, not because the past is invented.

a.q: Two historians describe frontier conflict in different words. What does this most likely show?
opts: They read the evidence with different questions or values
One of them believes the conflict did not take place
The facts of the conflict have changed over the years
One of them has misread some dates in the records
a.why: Different questions and values lead historians to explain the same past in different ways. A simple mistake with dates is possible, but disagreement usually comes from how evidence is chosen and explained, not from errors.
a.clue: Think about what each historian brings to the evidence.

b.q: Priya reads two books on a colonial town. One uses police records. The other uses oral histories from local families. They describe the same events very differently. What best explains this?
opts: Each author relied on sources showing a different viewpoint
Oral histories are stories, so they are not real evidence
One author has made up events that did not take place
The events changed after the police records were made
b.why: Police records and oral histories record the views of different people, so the books reach different interpretations. Oral histories are a kind of evidence, so dismissing them does not explain the difference.
b.clue: Compare whose view each type of source records.
